desc:
A traveller walks on an n x n grid from the top-left cell (0, 0) to the bottom-right cell (n-1, n-1), moving one step right or one step down at a time. The traveller must stay within w cells of the main diagonal: every visited cell (r, c) must satisfy |r - c| ≤ w.

Return the number of such routes modulo 1,000,000,007.

n = 3, w = 1  ->  4
n = 4, w = 1  ->  8
n = 4, w = 0  ->  0   (no route can stay on the diagonal)
n = 1, w = 0  ->  1
hints: Without the band restriction the count is a binomial coefficient, but the restriction removes cells in a pattern. A table over cells is natural.
Let ways[r][c] count routes ending in (r, c). Cells outside the band get 0, which forces every route to avoid them.
Only cells with max(0, r-w) ≤ c ≤ min(n-1, r+w) matter in row r, so each row needs at most 2w+1 updates. Keep a single array and zero the cell just left of the band when the band slides right.
editorial: Treat the cells outside the band exactly like obstacles: they hold 0 routes. For the other cells ways[r][c] = ways[r-1][c] + ways[r][c-1], with ways[0][0] = 1. A route is valid precisely when all its cells are inside the band, which the zeros guarantee.

With a single array of width n, row r is computed in place for the columns of the band only. When the band moves one column to the right, the value left over just outside its left edge (c = r - w - 1) must be cleared before it can leak into the next row. That visits O(n · min(n, w)) cells in total, at most O(n2), and uses O(n) space. For w ≥ n-1 the band is the whole grid and the answer is the binomial coefficient C(2n-2, n-1) modulo the prime.
